Subject: Calibration: exception cases, stack ranking, and next steps

Team —

Thanks for pulling the calibration packet together. I attached an updated matrix (calibration_matrix_2026_v2.xlsx) with the raw scores, current manager ratings, and my preliminary stack rank for the cross-functional ICs we discussed. There are five exception cases highlighted in red where manager recommendations diverge by more than one band.

Action items before we meet: 
- Please review the sheet and add a 1-2 line justification for any employee you flagged. Put those in the "Manager Notes" column.
- For the three people on the "high potential/low rating" row, add any concrete examples (projects, outcomes) you can cite.
- If you believe a calibration change requires promotion/comp plan impact, mark it and state the proposed adjustment.

We have the calibration sync scheduled for Wednesday. Olivia from Talent Advisors will join to observe and help surface bias signals. We'll keep this to 90 minutes and try to close the five exceptions in the doc. If we can't, we'll call a follow-up.

A few ground rules for the discussion: focus on outcome evidence, be explicit about recency/window (last 12 months), and avoid anchoring on previous year's rating. I expect each manager to come ready to state 1-2 evidence points.

Attachments: [Attachment: calibration_matrix_2026_v2.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 42KB)], [Attachment: manager_notes_flags.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

Thanks —
Evelyn

Evelyn —

Thanks, I reviewed the matrix and added short notes for the five exceptions in the Manager Notes column. Quick summary of my entries:
- Casey R.: flagged as high impact work in Q1 (latency rollout), but manager rating low due to mid-year delivery delays. I added two concrete project milestones that show consistent ownership; recommending rating uplift by one band and cohort mentoring for planning.
- J. Ortega: I included customer feedback excerpts that weigh toward consistent high quality. I think this is a difference of calibration style vs. consequence-based scoring. Recommend we keep same band but mark as stretch assignment candidate.
- T. Nguyen: marked as possible over-index for collaboration (peer feedback) but recent scope change warrants a conversation before adjusting comp.

I've also attached a one-page export (manager_notes_flags.pdf) with the full justifications. If it helps, I'll prepare a 3-slide summary for the meeting with the five cases.

Subject: Calibration wrap & immediate next steps (post-meeting notes)

Great session this morning — solid, evidence-focused conversation. Summary and immediate next steps: 

1) Decisions made (closed in meeting)
- Casey R.: rating increased by one band; comp uplift approved as discretionary increase (Finance to model delta).
- J. Ortega: no rating change; assigned to stretch assignment queue and flagged for leadership coaching.
- T. Nguyen: deferred — manager to sync with PM and return with concrete scope evidence by EOD Monday.

2) Open items requiring follow-up
- Finance modeling: Logan will share the budget delta table by EOD today.
- Comp impact approvals: send full list and proposed increases to Exec Compensation by Friday for final sign-off.
- Documentation: Marissa to produce the 3-slide summary and upload final matrix to Drive (link above).

3) Escalations & next steps for exceptions
- For any exception we still cannot close after manager follow-up, we'll add Olivia as an observer for bias review and schedule an arbitration call with Sarah Bennett from TalentOps.

I've updated the matrix with the final decisions and attached the post-meeting exported file. Please don't forward the attachment outside the recipients list — this remains confidential personnel information.

Thanks for moving quickly on this. We'll publish calibrated ratings to managers by next Wednesday (2026-06-03) and follow up on comp by the end of the pay cycle.

Evelyn
